title: He Turns the Brown to Green
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The ground was dry, the ground was brown,
with not one flower there;
then Isaiah told of water
and roses everywhere.

[Chorus]
Heavenly Father makes it bloom,
He turns the brown to green;
He fills the empty places up
with more than we have seen.

[Verse 2]
The desert woke and turned to green,
the dry place learned to sing;
the streams came splashing down the sand,
and every hill grew spring.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
When something good has gone all brown
and hope is hard to hold,
He waters it and warms it up
and green comes through the cold.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
The garden grows while no one looks,
the roots drink in the night;
and morning finds a hundred blooms
where brown had held so tight.

[Chorus]
mood: Opening music. A slow unfolding under the voice — one held note at the start of each line that quietly gathers a second and a third beneath it, the way a bare place fills in while nobody is watching. A small string quartet passing the melody between its players, warm and low, with a gentle rocking pull on the long lines. It travels from bare ground to green, each verse a little greener than the one before, and settles rather than ends.
